paper.title: Algorithm 911: Multiple-precision exponential integral and related functions (FM/ZM multiple-precision package, sample driver)

stack: Fortran 95 (TOMS 911 archive 911.zip: FM.f95, FMZM90.f95, fmsave.f95, SampleFM.f95, Doc/Makefile)

claim.text: SampleFM (author's sample driver) sample 2 prints the real root of x**5-3x**4+x**3-4x**2+x-6 to 500 decimal places; its double rounding 3.1206562153267265 agrees with the registered value to 1e-15 absolute.

values.name: real root of x**5-3x**4+x**3-4x**2+x-6 (SampleFM.out sample 2, 500-digit value rounded to double; the first 16 significant digits are 3.120656215326726)

attempt: Reproduced in both passes. The authors' Doc/Makefile cannot run as shipped: it looks for FM.f95, FMZM90.f95, fmsave.f95 and SampleFM.f95 in its own directory, but the archive puts them in Fortran95/Src and Fortran95/Drivers, so make stops at 'No rule to make target fmsave.f95' (G1 original attempt logged). Build (basis patched, build-only): the Makefile's own rules are run unedited from a separate output directory with VPATH pointing at the unedited source tree, gfortran -O3 on the command line. Pass 1 (-O3) and pass 2 (no optimisation flags, clean directory) both print a sample 2 root whose first 80 digits match the shipped SampleFM.out and whose double value is 3.1206562153267265, equal to the registered value.

original_attempt.reason: make in the archive's Doc directory stops at 'No rule to make target fmsave.f95': the Makefile expects the sources beside it, and the archive does not ship makefile.inc (compiler not set) either. Nothing compiles as shipped.
